subject.title: improve(gateway): tunable control-plane write rate limit, default unchanged

question: Should OpenClaw expose a gateway-global 1–600 control-plane write budget that any authorized configuration administrator can raise for all client identities?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but the permanent quota granularity and maximum determine how much an existing security hardening boundary may be weakened; repository evidence cannot establish that policy intent.

options.title: Accept the bounded global knob
options.body: Approve the current model because the safe default and identity buckets remain unchanged and operators receive explicit security guidance.

options.title: Require scoped automation capacity
options.body: Replace the global dial with an auth-class or identity-scoped mechanism so trusted automation can burst without weakening every caller.

options.title: Keep the fixed limiter
options.body: Decline the new configuration surface and require operators to batch atomic changes or redesign provisioning around the existing budget.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded global knob
recommendation.body: Approve the current model because the safe default and identity buckets remain unchanged and operators receive explicit security guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes a shipped gateway security safeguard and public configuration surface, areas most closely connected to this person's release and gateway ownership history.
